subject: Region locking options and interim cross-border transfer windows
messages:
From: Megan Lowe <megan.lowe@healthlycare.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Region-locking commitments + a few DPA clarifications

Hi Rishi / Laura,

Thanks for walking us through the platform last week. We have a short list of items the legal and security teams asked me to confirm before we proceed with a Hosted purchase order:

- Can Redwood commit to region locking for customer production traffic (EU only) as a contractual term, and if so, how is that enforced operationally?
- In the DPA the clause about "transient cross-border processing" is permissive; what triggers a transient hop (planned maintenance, unplanned failover, analytics backfill, support sessions)?
- What is the maximum duration of any temporary cross-border processing window you would accept in the contract?
- Is customer-managed KMS an option for EU-only customers?
- Please attach the current subprocessor roster and an example of an operational runbook describing failover behavior.

I've attached an annotated spreadsheet with line items (HC_DPA_Questions.xlsx). Procurement is on copy for timeline constraints. Ideally we want concrete answers we can insert in a DPA addendum rather than vague promises.

Best,
Megan Lowe
Head of Security Operations
HealthlyCare, Inc.

Attachments: HC_DPA_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet with line items)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Lowe <megan.lowe@healthlycare.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Region-locking commitments + a few DPA clarifications

Megan — thanks for the detailed list. I pulled together answers below and attached our operational runbook and a current subprocessor export so you have concrete artifacts to review.

1) Region-locking commitment: we can contractually commit to "region affinity" for production request processing and persistent storage (EU region), with the following operational model:
   - Primary affinity: customer tenant is pinned to our EU serving fleet and EU-backed storage by default.
   - Fallback policy: in the event of catastrophic region outage, we allow a controlled, timebound transfer to a pre-authorized failover region. That pathway is subject to the failover triggers below.

2) Triggers for transient cross-border processing:
   - Planned maintenance with advance notice (we propose 72h notice for non-emergency maintenance).
   - Emergency failover when availability on the primary EU fleet is below defined SLOs and recovery cannot be achieved within X minutes.
   - Short-lived analytics/telemetry replay necessary for debugging when that activity cannot be performed on EU-only tooling.
   - Ad-hoc support session by a vetted operator (must be requested and logged).

3) Maximum duration: our standard hosted contract offers a 72-hour maximum for any transient cross-border processing window without explicit customer sign-off. For customers that require stricter bounds we offer two pathways:
   - Option A: EU-only Dedicated/Private deployment (no transient hops to other regions unless customer explicitly authorizes in writing).
   - Option B: Hosted with a reduced transient window (48 hours) plus an automated notification and escalation flow for every event.

4) Customer-managed KMS: Yes — available for Dedicated and Private deployments today. For Hosted customers we offer a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow for envelope keys; full key isolation (HSM-backed customer keys used for all persistent data) requires Dedicated or Private.

5) Subprocessors & runbook: attached 'subprocessors_2027-06.csv' shows current subprocessors and data paths; 'redwood-region-runbook-v2.pdf' is the operational artifact describing the failover playbook.

Next steps: if HealthlyCare wants the EU-only contractual guarantee, we should evaluate whether Dedicated capacity or Private deployment is required based on traffic, KMS needs, and SLA. Happy to map costs once you confirm which option you prefer.

Proposed time for a short follow-up call: Tue 8 Jun, 9–11 AM CET or Wed 9 Jun, 2–4 PM CET. Let me know which slot suits you.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Security Programs | Redwood Inference

+1 415 555 0189

From: Megan Lowe <megan.lowe@healthlycare.com>

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 08:44:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Region-locking commitments + a few DPA clarifications

Thanks Rishi — very helpful. A couple of quick follow-ups: 

- For the 72-hour standard: is that measured from the time of failover start or from the time you notify customers? We need to ensure the clock starts when processing leaves the EU.
- For analytics / telemetry replay: can you confirm whether telemetry replays can be scoped to pseudonymized payloads for Hosted customers to avoid content-level transfer?
- BYOK for Hosted: can you share the encryption envelope flow diagram? We need to understand which tokens/keys are ever in Redwood-managed KMS.

Procurement is pushing for the hosted path if we can get a 48-hour hard cap and an explicit subprocessor obligation (30 days advance notice for new subprocessors impacting EU routing). Can you confirm Redwood can accept that in an addendum or whether this requires Dedicated/Private?

If it helps, procurement has a short checklist and would like answers by EOD Wed 9 Jun to keep the purchase order on track.

—Megan

Attachments referenced: none

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Lowe <megan.lowe@healthlycare.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, procurement@healthlycare.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Region-locking commitments + a few DPA clarifications

Megan — quick clarifications inline: 

- 72-hour measurement: we measure from the time production request routing leaves the primary EU serving fabric (i.e., first packet processed outside EU). Notification to customers is automated within minutes; the 72-hour cap is independent of notification latency. We can add explicit contract language to that effect.

- Telemetry replays: for Hosted customers we support scoped pseudonymization for operational telemetry. Sensitive payloads are redacted before any cross-region replay by default; full-content replays require customer approval. We'll include the pseudonymization checklist in the addendum.

- BYOK envelope flow: attached is a short diagram and description in the runbook; in short: customer envelope keys are used to wrap persistent datastore keys. A minimal set of ephemeral keys for runtime inference must remain in the runtime memory; these are never persisted to Redwood-managed KMS in Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted BYOK the envelope unwrap occurs in a limited HSM boundary we manage — we'll share the exact sequence diagram for procurement review.

- Subprocessor notice: we can accept a 30-day advance notice requirement for subprocessors that materially affect EU routing for Hosted customers, provided we can keep a limited operational exception for emergency security patches (we'll notify within 48h in those rare cases). If HealthlyCare requires zero-exception subprocessors, that maps to Private deployment.

To keep procurement on schedule: we will produce a redline DPA addendum with the EU-affinity language, 48-hour hosted transient cap, 30-day subprocessor notice, and the telemetry pseudonymization checklist by EOD Wed 9 Jun. If that meets your checklist, procurement can proceed with the hosted PO. Otherwise we should move to a dedicated scoping call to size Dedicated/Private.

I'll draft the addendum today and circulate to Laura to run through legal.

Thanks — talk soon.
Rishi

Attachments: redwood-region-runbook-v2.pdf (contains envelope flow summary); subprocessors_2027-06.csv
